ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based PEP and sanctions screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against (i) the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit PEP database; (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List as implemented in New Zealand under the United Nations Act 1946 and the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002; (iv) the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade autonomous sanctions designations; and (v) the EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists. Screening must be recalibrated at intervals not exceeding 90 days, and enhanced customer due diligence, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, is mandatory for PEPs, beneficial owners resident in high-risk third countries, and complex offshore structures pursuant to Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, sections 22 to 27.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register administered by the New Zealand Companies Office (a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment), accessible at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A proposed company name must be expressed in English or te reo Māori using Latin-script characters (A-Z), Arabic numerals (0-9), and permitted punctuation only. Non-Latin scripts, including Hanzi/Chinese characters, Cyrillic, or Arabic script, are not registerable as the legal name; the legal name must be transliterated into Roman characters, and any Chinese or other foreign-language trading name may be recorded only as an alternative business name after the registered Latin-character name has been cleared.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Limited (absent Registrar consent for approved overseas special-status usage)
New Zealand (where implying official sponsorship or Crown connection)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory extension of the reservation is available; if incorporation is not completed within 20 working days, the reservation lapses and a fresh application must be submitted. Upon rejection under Companies Act 1993, sections 20 to 22, the applicant or its registered agent may: (1) lodge a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies within 10 working days of the rejection notice, addressing the identical-or-almost-identical or objectionable-name grounds relied upon; (2) if reconsideration is declined, appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016; and (3) in parallel, re-submit an alternative cleared name through the Companies Register portal to avoid operational delay. Registrar decisions are reviewable for error of law, unreasonableness, or breach of natural justice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially acceptable. A serviced virtual-office arrangement is recognized provided it delivers a genuine physical street address in New Zealand at which legal process may be served during ordinary business hours and from which the company's statutory records can be produced upon demand. A post office box or digital mail-forwarding address alone does not satisfy section 189 of the Companies Act 1993. Because the entity operates in the ISIC 8299 registered agent and offshore secretarial services class (Medium Risk Enhanced), the registered office provider must itself be a licensed trust and company service provider registered on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register and supervised for AML/CFT compliance by the Department of Internal Affairs.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated-moderate. As a trust and company service provider and registered-agent operator classified Medium Risk Enhanced, the quantified likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Department of Internal Affairs, or of a mandated audit by the appointed AML/CFT supervisor, within the first 36 months of operation is estimated at 25-35%. This assessment reflects the Department of Internal Affairs supervisory strategy favoring targeted, intelligence-led inspections of corporate secretarial providers administering offshore structures.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 2020–2023; applicable provisions include ss 9–14 (constitution), s 20 (name requirements), ss 38–40 (registration of companies), s 39 (application for registration), s 40 (registration and certificate of incorporation), ss 42–47 (allotment and issue of shares), s 60 (registered office), ss 83–84 (register of shares), s 91 (board resolutions in lieu of meeting), ss 128–130 (appointment of directors), and ss 189–199 (directors' duties). Subsidiary instruments: Companies (Fees) Regulations 2016, Companies (Directors and Registered Offices) Regulations 1993, and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 for registered agent and secretarial services.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the New Zealand Companies Register and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) portal at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCN1 — 'Application for Registration of a Company Limited by Shares' submitted electronically under s 39 of the Companies Act 1993, together with the company constitution, subscriber consents, director consents, registered office details, and the prescribed filing fee on the Companies Office Online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an International Company (IC) incorporated as a company limited by shares under the Companies Act 1993. Each subscriber must take at least one share (s 39(2)(a)); shares may be issued partly or fully paid (ss 42–45). No escrow account, capital deposit, or bank verification is required at incorporation. Shares may be allotted for cash or non-cash consideration (s 47), including property and goodwill, at fair value as approved by board resolution. Where the company holds client monies for secretarial and registered-agent services, such client funds must be maintained in separately designated trust or client accounts in accordance with the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006 (if applicable), but this does not constitute a paid-up capital escrow requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [CK_IC] INTERNATIONAL COMPANY LIMITED (NZBN: [•]). ADOPTED in writing by the duly-constituted first director and the subscriber shareholders on [•] at [Registered Office], New Zealand, pursuant to s 91(2) of the Companies Act 1993 ('the Act'). UNANIMOUS RESOLUTIONS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION — THAT the company be incorporated with [1,000] ordinary shares of no par value, being the entire authorized and issued share capital; THAT the subscribers severally subscribe for the Shares detailed in the subscription schedule to this resolution at a consideration of NZD [•] in cash (or such non-cash property valued at fair value, as the case may be); THAT such consideration constitute fully-paid value for the Shares in accordance with ss 42, 45, and 47 of the Act; THAT the Shares be allotted and issued forthwith, entered in the register of shareholders under ss 83–84 of the Act, and that the subscription proceeds be applied to the working capital of the company without requirement of any escrow account, the Act imposing no minimum paid-up capital threshold. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION — THAT the registered office of the company be and is hereby fixed at [street address, city, postcode, New Zealand], a physical address in New Zealand at which documents may be served and notices delivered in accordance with s 60 of the Act; THAT the Registrar of Companies be notified of the registered office address and any subsequent change under s 60(2); and THAT the registered office shall house the company's statutory registers, share register, constitution, and board minutes. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS — THAT the following officers be and are hereby appointed to hold office from the close of this resolution: (a) [Name], sole Director and Chair; (b) [Name], Chief Executive Officer; (c) [Name], Company Secretary and designated AML/CFT Compliance Officer under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; and (d) [Name], Registered Agent in charge of client onboarding, statutory records, and offshore secretarial administration; THAT each appointed officer has executed a Consent to Act as Officer and provided verification documents for the Companies Register; and THAT the Director be authorized to open and operate bank accounts, sign banking mandates, instruct legal counsel, and execute tax and regulatory filings on behalf of the company. 4. REGISTERED AGENT AND SECRETARIAL BUSINESS MANDATE — THAT the company adopt the statutory company secretarial and commercial registered agent business model (ISIC 8299 / NAICS 541199); THAT the initial AML/CFT risk assessment and compliance programme for a trust and company service provider be adopted as tabled, subject to registration with the Department of Internal Affairs; and THAT client engagements be accepted only after satisfactory customer due diligence, including beneficial-ownership verification, source-of-funds review, and enhanced measures for any offshore vehicle or high-risk jurisdiction. 5. GENERAL AUTHORISATION — THAT the Director be and is hereby vested with full power to execute, deliver, and file all documents, pay all fees, obtain all licenses, appoint local professional advisers, and do all acts necessary to give full effect to the foregoing resolutions. CERTIFIED AS A TRUE AND CORRECT COPY: [Signature] — [Name], Director and Chair. Date: [•].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Online Name Reservation Service and NZBN portal (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that the proposed International Company name, including the mandatory suffix 'Limited', is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and is not prohibited under s 20 of the Companies Act 1993 (no offensive, official-Crown, or incorporated-society name). Reserve the approved name online for up to 20 working days and record the reservation reference for use in the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (including 'Limited' suffix)
Name search and availability certificate from the Companies Register
IPONZ trademark clearance report (recommended)
Customer instruction to proceed with name reservation
Anti-money-laundering identity verification evidence of the subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar flags the name as prohibited or similar under s 21 of the Act, file a written submission supporting registration, propose an alternative name to the client, and re-submit the reservation application without losing the incorporation priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Constitution and Corporate Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand-qualified solicitor or chartered accountant; document upload to NZ Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the company constitution satisfying s 29 of the Companies Act 1993 and addressing share capital, director powers, quorum, voting, registered office, and indemnity clauses; prepare subscriber application forms, consent to act as director, consent to act as company secretary or compliance officer, and the register of shareholders pro forma. Certify that the constitution does not derogate from the fundamental protections in ss 36–40 of the Act. Deliver the final board-approved pack for execution.
required_dossiers: Company Constitution (s 29-compliant)
Subscriber consent and share application form
Consent to Act as Director (Form NZCN2 equivalent)
Consent to Act as Company Secretary or Compliance Officer
Shareholder register pro forma
AML/CFT customer due diligence file for the shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns a query on the constitution (e.g., inconsistent delegation or entrenchment clauses), amend the constitution by ordinary resolution under s 31, re-execute, and re-file with a certification of the amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment of Application for Registration (Form NZCN1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Online portal (RealMe-authenticated filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form NZCN1 through the Companies Online portal, entering the reserved name, registered office address, director and shareholder details, share structure, and constitution; upload scanned executed consents; attest that all information is true and complete under s 39(3); and pay the official filing fee of NZD 170.00 (GST incl.) by credit card or bank wire through the portal's payment gateway.
required_dossiers: Form NZCN1 — Application for Registration of a Company
Reserved name reference number
Certified copy of the company constitution
Director consent forms and identity evidence
Subscriber consent forms and identity evidence
Registered office address proof (e.g., lease or land registry extract)
Payment receipt / bank wire confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended for a defect under s 40A, the Registrar issues a notice of correction; the applicant has 5 working days to remedy the defect online. If the application is rejected, re-lodge with a written explanation addressing each query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and Post-incorporation Statutory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies — New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance of Form NZCN1, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and allocates the NZBN and company number. The company must then file the first board resolution, register the directors and any significant control information within 10 working days, and maintain the share register, directors' register, and minute book at the registered office. Confirm the registered office address in the Companies Register and update any officer changes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
First Board Resolution minutes (s 91(2))
Register of Directors (Form NZCN3)
Register of Shareholders
Notice of registered office (if separate notification required)
NZBN certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation is not issued within the published SLA, escalate to the MBIE Companies Office customer contact centre. If the certificate contains a clerical error, apply for correction under s 53A of the Act within 15 working days; administrative rectification is issued free of further state fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (IRD Number) and Financial Service Provider Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue (New Zealand) — Business Registration Service; Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for FSP Act registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated company for a New Zealand Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number through the Business Registration Service, confirming the NZBN linkage; apply for GST registration if the company expects to supply taxable services above NZD 60,000 per annum or elects voluntary registration; complete income-tax registration and any required withholding tax registration for non-resident shareholders. Concurrently, assess whether the registered agent and secretarial services constitute 'regulated financial services' under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; if so, register on the FSP register and join an approved dispute resolution scheme within the statutory deadline.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN certificate
IRD registration application (BRR form through Business Registration)
Director and beneficial-owner identity documents (photo ID and proof of address)
FSP Act registration application
Approved dispute resolution scheme membership confirmation (if applicable)
AML/CFT compliance programme summary for licensing assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue queries the NZBN or IRD linkage, resolve through the myIR secure messaging and provide a corrected IRD application. If the FMA refuses FSP registration, appeal the decision to the District Court under the FSP Act and continue AML/CFT registration with DIA, which is the primary licensing gate for registered agent services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/CFT Reporting Entity Registration and Compliance Officer Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) — AML/CFT Supervision Team
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the DIA Reporting Entity Registration application for a 'trust and company service provider' under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Attach the entity's AML/CFT risk assessment (business risk, customer risk, country risk, and delivery-channel risk) and the full written compliance programme, including customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence, beneficial-ownership verification, ongoing monitoring, suspicious transaction reporting, record-keeping, and the appointment of a compliance officer. Complete DIA's online readiness assessment and keep a copy of the registration certificate at the registered office.
required_dossiers: DIA AML/CFT reporting entity registration form
AML/CFT risk assessment document (risk rating and matrix)
AML/CFT compliance programme (full policy manual)
Compliance officer appointment resolution and CV
Business continuity and record-retention policy (5-year minimum retention)
Staff training log and competency attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIA issues a remediation notice under s 78 of the AML/CFT Act requiring further information, respond within 10 working days with supplementary documents; if registration is declined, remedy the compliance gaps, resubmit, or apply for internal review, and in the interim restrict operations to non-AML/CFT administrative services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises Occupational, Fire Safety, Building, and Civil Defence Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial Authority (City or District Council Building Control); Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); WorkSafe New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) under the Building Act 2004 for the registered office premises, including an annual compliance schedule statement covering fire escape routes, smoke detection, emergency lighting, and any automatic systems; arrange a Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) fire safety inspection; carry out a structural load assessment for the record archive; notify WorkSafe of the office as a place of work and adopt a health-and-safety policy, first-aid provisions, and an emergency evacuation / civil-defence plan. Secure professional indemnity and office insurance before client engagements commence.
required_dossiers: Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) certificate
Annual building compliance schedule statement under s 108 Building Act 2004
Fire safety inspection certificate / FENZ compliance letter
Structural floor-load assessment for record storage areas
WorkSafe notice of place of work (where applicable)
Health and safety induction register and emergency evacuation plan
Professional indemnity insurance certificate
Civil-defence emergency signage and supplies checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BWOF is refused or a 'Notice to Fix' is issued, correct the building defects, obtain a new building consent inspection, and reapply; a temporary waiver under s 35 of the Building Act 2004 may be sought from the territorial authority. Pending compliance, operate the client-facing secretarial function from a compliant virtual registered office and remote data centre, ensuring no personnel are physically present in non-complying areas.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) — AML/CFT Supervision Group as the primary industrial licensing body for trust and company service providers; New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE) as the corporate registry authority; Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) and the territorial authority for physical premises clearance; no manufacturing or industrial production board applies because the ISIC 8299 registered agent and offshore secretarial activity is office-based professional administration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Reporting Entity Registration Certificate under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 for Trust and Company Service Providers; Certificate of Incorporation under the Companies Act 1993; and, where applicable, Financial Service Provider Registration Certificate under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority New Zealand (EPA) in coordination with the territorial authority (city or district council) under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — No Environmental Impact Assessment required. Office-based corporate secretarial, registered agent, and statutory administration services are not listed in Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991; the activity does not involve industrial land use, earthworks, discharge to air or water, or significant natural hazard exposure, and therefore no resource consent or EIA report is triggered under ss 9 and 14 of the RMA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge is generated by the registered agent activity. Office wastewater must connect to the municipal sewerage network and comply with the local council's trade-waste bylaw for suspended solids and BOD within domestic tolerance limits. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from low-volume laser printing and document shredding are de minimis and exempt under the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality 2004 (NES-AQ); any future bulk printing must achieve VOC emission limits of no greater than 80 mg/m³ for offset processes. All electronic waste, including secure-destruction hard drives, must be disposed through certified e-waste recyclers under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, and any confidential waste incineration is prohibited without a resource consent under the RMA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: annual Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) under the Building Act 2004, including means of escape, smoke detection, fire extinguisher inspection by a chartered fire safety engineer, and emergency lighting verification by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ). Structural load clearance: a building consent memorandum from the territorial authority confirming the floor load-bearing capacity (minimum 3.5 kPa uniformly distributed for office records and archive vaults). Workplace clearance: WorkSafe New Zealand health-and-safety induction, first-aid registers, safe work method statements for manual handling, and a civil-defence emergency plan (earthquake-prone building status, safe-location signage, and evacuation assembly point) — all required before personnel are physically present for client services.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake) — the Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand. Digital portal: myIR, accessible at https://www.ird.govt.nz (secure sign-in at https://myir.ird.govt.nz); business registry interface via the NZBN (New Zealand Business Number) Register at https://www.nzbn.govt.nz.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign company, including a Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) operating a registered agent and offshore secretarial office with a New Zealand presence, must first obtain an NZBN (optional for non-resident companies) and then apply to Inland Revenue for a single IRD number which functions as the company tax identification number for income tax, GST, and PAYE. Application is made by filing form IR742 (Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application) — or, where the company is registered on the New Zealand Companies Register, the IRD number is issued automatically through the NZBN registration event — accompanied by (i) a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation issued by the Registrar of International Companies in the Cook Islands (or equivalent foreign company registry), (ii) the constitutive documents (Articles/Charter and Memorandum of Association), (iii) a list of directors, shareholders and the registered office address, (iv) a completed IR596 Certificate of Identification or equivalent evidence for the beneficial owners, and (v) details of the New Zealand appointed agent/service address. Where the CK_IC activities create a taxable activity in New Zealand (e.g., fees earned for secretarial services physically performed in New Zealand), a separate GST registration must be completed online via myIR or on form IR356 (GST registration). The IRD number is issued within 8–12 working days for paper applications and is required before any New Zealand bank account, payroll, or Customs client code can be operationalized. If the CK_IC merely uses a licensed New Zealand registered agent as an outsourced service provider and itself has no New Zealand taxable activity, the CK_IC is not required to register for NZ tax; the New Zealand agent must separately register for GST and IRD number in its own name.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no check-the-box election. A non-resident CK_IC is taxed solely on New Zealand-sourced income on a territorial basis (Income Tax Act 2007, Schedule 6 and s YD 4), with no tax on foreign offshore secretarial revenue unless central management and control is exercised in New Zealand. The Cook Islands International Companies Act tax exemption (0% on offshore income) does not extend to New Zealand-sourced income. Relevant elections and regimes include: (i) GST group registration (s 55, GST Act 1985) permitting consolidation of resident group companies; (ii) GST cash-basis or payment-basis accounting elections (ss 19C and 19D); (iii) hybrid and branch mismatch rules in Part FH, requiring a New Zealand deduction-taker to eliminate double non-taxation where the CK_IC payer is tax-exempt (an electable adjusting amount methodology applies under the Financial Arrangements Rules in s FH 6-FH 8); (iv) foreign currency elections for financial arrangements under s EW 14; and (v) the limited look-through company (LTC) election is unavailable because the CK_IC is not a New Zealand-resident qualifying company. Non-resident companies receiving only New Zealand interest or dividends may elect for approved issuer levy (AIL) status under ss 32M-32R of the Stamp and Cheque Duties Act 1971 (non-applicable to service fees).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), a value-added consumption tax imposed under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of annual taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) made in the course of a New Zealand taxable activity within any 12-month period. The same NZD 60,000 threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of remote services (including digital, professional, registered-agent, and secretarial services) where supplies are made to New Zealand-resident recipients; once the threshold is exceeded on a trailing 12-month look-back, registration is compulsory, with a prospectively effective date and no retrospective liability.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, government API pre-clearance, or digital stamping regime applies. New Zealand operates a self-assessment e-invoicing model under the PEPPOL (Pan-European Public Procurement OnLine) framework, PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0; e-invoicing is voluntary for commerce, but all central government agencies must receive e-invoices through an accredited PEPPOL Access Point and the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) maintains the NZ e-Invoicing infrastructure. GST returns are filed via myIR on monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly cycles; payments are due in full by the return filing date. Invoices issued under s 24 of the GST Act 1985 must contain the words tax invoice, the supplier's name, IRD/GST number, date of issue, description, quantity and price. Records, including the PEPPOL e-invoice XML files and any digital clearance logs, must be retained for 7 years (TAA 1994, s 51).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% GST applies under s 11 of the GST Act 1985 where the supplier ships goods out of New Zealand and exports them (or causes their export) within 28 days of the time of supply; where goods are delivered to a port or airport in New Zealand for the purpose of being shipped, the export must be completed within 28 days of the delivery date, and the supplier must hold satisfactory evidence of export. Services: 0% GST applies under s 11A to services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, unless the services are supplied directly in connection with (i) land in New Zealand; (ii) movable personal property situated in New Zealand (except goods exported or for repair/processing); or (iii) physical services performed in New Zealand for the direct benefit of an individual present in New Zealand. Registered-agent and offshore corporate secretarial services supplied to Cook Islands International Companies (CK_IC) whose directors, registered office, and central management sit outside New Zealand qualify for zero-rating only where the services are performed outside New Zealand; secretarial work physically performed by staff in New Zealand is standard-rated unless it falls within the s 11A(1)(e) remote-services carve-out for a non-resident recipient. The taxpayer must obtain and retain: CK_IC certificate of incorporation and tax-exempt certificate, copy of the service agreement indicating offshore performance, confirmation of non-resident status (registered office in Rarotonga/Aitutaki; non-resident director declarations), and evidence that the CK_IC derives no New Zealand-source income.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CusDEC) filed through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window and the Customs export clearance report
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand (for goods)
GST tax invoice issued under s 24 of the GST Act 1985
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency bank credit advice evidencing settlement of the export receivable
Non-resident status evidence of the CK_IC (certificate of incorporation, registered office certificate, tax exemption confirmation from the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission)
Executed offshore service agreement and performance records locating the place of supply outside New Zealand (for services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue audits zero-rating claims with particular focus on related-party cross-border services, sham offices, and round-tripping structures involving tax-exempt Cook Islands ICs. Where zero-rating is incorrectly claimed, the supplier is liable for the uncollected output GST, denial of corresponding input credits, use-of-money interest at the prescribed quarterly underpayment rate, and shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for failing to take reasonable care (s 141B), 20% for an unacceptable tax position (s 141C), 40% for gross carelessness (s 141D), 100% for an abusive tax position (s 141E), and 150% for evasion (s 141EB). The general anti-avoidance rule (s BG1 Income Tax Act 2007; s 76 GST Act 1985) permits the Commissioner to reconstruct the arrangement retrospectively, clawing back refunded GST with up to 4 years' retrospectivity for non-disclosure. Criminal prosecution under s 143A (evasion) carries a fine up to NZD 200,000 for a body corporate and/or up to 5 years' imprisonment for individuals; fraudulent GST refund claims may also be prosecuted under s 228 of the Crimes Act 1961 (up to 7 years' imprisonment). New Zealand has no statutory export-proceeds repatriation deadline; however, the 180-day period is used by Inland Revenue as a commercial benchmark — export invoices remaining unsettled beyond 180 days without explanation are treated as not genuinely exported and the zero-rating is clawed back. For associated-party offshore service fees, failure to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (ss GC1-GC14, OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines) triggers a documentation penalty of NZD 20,000 (first request) and NZD 50,000 (each subsequent request) in addition to any transfer pricing adjustment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua); foreign exchange administration is fully liberalised, with no separate exchange control department requiring general approvals. The Financial Markets Authority (FMA) regulates financial service providers and conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully convertible currency under an open capital account. Current account items, capital transactions, profit repatriation, dividends, liquidation proceeds, and service contract payments are freely transferable in any currency without prior central bank approval. Non-residents may hold New Zealand dollar and foreign-currency accounts with registered banks. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 may apply only to certain 'sensitive' land and significant business assets acquisitions; ordinary treasury transactions for a registered agent/corporate secretarial services entity are not restricted. There are no profit remittance hurdles beyond standard taxation and CRS/FATCA self-certification compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Service providers and exporters may retain receipts in any currency, hold foreign-currency accounts, and remit or convert NZD freely in accordance with commercial requirements. The Reserve Bank imposes no obligation to convert export service earnings into New Zealand dollars.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited, New Zealand Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is Medium for ancillary treasury operations, but Low as a substitute for a licensed bank relationship. New Zealand-incorporated financial service providers may be registered under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and must be supervised under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Non-bank payment service providers may offer virtual accounts, payment initiation, and SWIFT-style disbursements but cannot take deposits, do not have Payment NZ clearing membership, and are not authorised as banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021. Offshore EMIs face significant legal constraints: they are generally not licensed deposit-takers in New Zealand and must rely on New Zealand partner banks for local clearing; many cannot provide NZD Direct Debit/Credit via the Payments NZ bulk electronic clearing system or real-time ESAS settlement. A registered agent should establish a primary banking relationship with a tier-1 bank and use EMIs only for multi-currency receivables or disbursement convenience.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand banks generally permit remote account opening for companies, including International Companies, using electronic identity verification and certified corporate documents. However, because this business scope involves company secretarial and registered agent services with a medium-risk enhanced rating, banks typically require a video interview or physical appointment for at least one director, authorised signatory, or senior compliance officer. Fully remote, non-interactive onboarding is not currently available at tier-1 New Zealand banks. The compliance mandate includes verification of the beneficial ownership chain, confirmation that the applicant holds the necessary statutory licence (where applicable), source-of-funds documentation, and a clear written AML/CFT compliance programme. Physical presence of all directors is not required, but the bank's AML/CFT officer may require a physical appearance if the structure is complex or UBO documentation is not readily verifiable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company with non-resident owners and nominee or registered agent shareholding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Companies Office extract showing certificate of incorporation, registered office, directors, and shareholders; ownership structure chart tracing all natural-person beneficial owners; certified copies of passports and proof of residential address of all directors/UBOs; certified board resolutions authorising account opening and signatories; source of wealth/source of funds documentation; professional references from a regulated lawyer or accountant; CRS self-certification and FATCA forms; and a written business plan describing the registered agent and corporate secretarial services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border fee collection by credit card and bank wire with high-volume, low-value transactions typical of company formation and secretarial services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT risk assessment covering the business model; customer risk rating methodology; transaction monitoring systems calibrated to detect unusual patterns and structuring; detailed client service agreements and engagement letters; sample invoices and proof of service delivery; sanctions and PEP screening procedures; staff training records; and an independent audit or compliance review report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fiduciary or escrow-like handling of statutory filing fees and government disbursements where the company receives client funds earmarked for the Companies Office or other authorities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trust account or separate client disbursement account ledger; flow-of-funds policy; underlying statutory fee schedules; client instructions for each disbursement; reconciliation statements; prohibition on unlicensed deposit-taking or lending; professional indemnity insurance certificate; and a legal opinion confirming the arrangement does not constitute a financial product under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners resident in high-risk jurisdictions or countries subject to international sanctions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening logs covering UN, OFAC, EU, UK and New Zealand sanctions lists; jurisdiction-specific risk assessment; legitimate business rationale documentation; enhanced due diligence including accredited independent professional references; certified identification documents and proof of address; tax identification numbers and tax residence certificates; and a legal opinion confirming economic substance and legitimate non-tax purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained structuring of cash-like, same-day round deposits, or use of electronic funds transfer rails that obscure the underlying business purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT transaction monitoring policy; real-time alerts and exception reports; suspicious transaction escalation procedure; customer interviews and written explanations; reconstructed business records showing the underlying corporate secretarial transactions; internal suspicious activity reports and submissions to the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections to the New Zealand International Company are routed by SWIFT MT103 from the overseas shareholder or lender. No exchange control approval is required. The remittance must clearly state the business purpose code (e.g., 'Equity Capital' or 'Intercompany Loan') and reference the New Zealand Companies Office company number. The receiving bank will require a certified copy of the share subscription resolution or intercompany loan agreement, a completed source of funds declaration, and CRS/FATCA self-certification forms. Funds must be received in the entity's NZD or foreign-currency operational account; for client trust money, a segregated client account must be used. The bank will verify that the remitter account name matches the shareholder/UBO documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements are cleared using: (i) Payments NZ's bulk electronic clearing system (BECS) for NZD domestic and trans-Tasman periodic payments; (ii) the Reserve Bank's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) for high-value real-time gross settlement; (iii) SWIFT MT103 for single cross-border wire transfers; and (iv) documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) for international trade settlements governed by UCP 600. The entity's bank may issue a commercial LC for the settlement of goods/services on behalf of clients where trade finance facilities are established. All cross-border payments require a valid purpose code and may trigger correspondent bank due diligence; payments to sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions will be blocked. Trade disbursements must be supported by invoices, contracts, and the bank's AML/CFT screening outputs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, NZD/AUD, NZD/JPY) offered by New Zealand registered banks for hedging committed fee income or disbursement expenses.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted currencies that cannot be settled deliverable onshore, executed with a licensed bank or authorised financial product provider.
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and plain-vanilla cross-currency interest rate swaps) for aligning FX risk on medium-term liquidity and matching the currency of fee receivables.
European-style FX options (simple puts/calls) to hedge forecast foreign-currency cash flows, provided they are not used for speculative trading.
Foreign-currency accounts (multi-currency accounts) as natural treasury hedging mechanisms allowing fee receipts and disbursements in the same currency without conversion.
Plain-vanilla interest rate swaps or forward rate agreements to hedge NZD interest rate risk on any bank credit facilities (non-speculative).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies — New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: due on or before the 30th calendar day after the company's annual return date (anniversary of incorporation); the electronic filing window opens 30 days before that date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a NZD 200 (approx. USD 124) late-filing penalty in addition to the base fee. Non-filing for two consecutive annual returns triggers administrative strike-off under Section 318 of the Companies Act 1993; each director is also liable to an offence-level fine of up to NZD 10,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Annual Re-confirmation (Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Act 2021)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (filed electronically in the same submission as the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within the Annual Return filing window; an interim notification of any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 10 working days of the company becoming aware of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence carrying a maximum fine of NZD 50,000 for the company and NZD 10,000 per responsible director; the Registrar may suspend processing of any transaction or annual return until the register is rectified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements and Audit Report Filing (Financial Reporting Act 2013; Companies Act 1993, Section 210) — mandatory only if audit/filing thresholds are crossed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies — New Zealand Companies Office (for large companies); Financial Markets Authority (FMA) (for FMC reporting entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the company's balance date (31 March for standard-reporting NZ companies; non-standard balance dates may be adopted with Registrar approval).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is a criminal offence under Section 54 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013; each director is liable on conviction to a fine of up to NZD 50,000. Continued default may additionally ground strike-off proceedings by the Registrar and adverse enforcement action by the FMA.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit and financial statement filing are compulsory for (i) FMC reporting entities under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; (ii) 'large' companies exceeding at least two of three thresholds: total assets NZD 60 million (approx. USD 37 million), total revenue NZD 30 million (approx. USD 18.6 million), and 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees; and (iii) companies whose constitution, shareholders' resolution (representing at least 10% of voting rights), or parent undertaking requires an audit. A tax-exempt offshore international company engaged in registered-agent services is ordinarily below these thresholds and is exempt from both audit and filing unless a threshold is crossed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with NZ GAAP as prescribed by the External Reporting Board (XRB): NZ IFRS (Tier 1); NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2); or the NZ IFRS Simplified Reporting Framework (Tier 3/4) for non-reporting small entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every New Zealand company must maintain a private beneficial ownership register recording each 'significant individual' holding 25% or more of voting shares or ultimate control. The appointed registered agent (acting as a Trust and Company Service Provider) must apply customer due diligence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 to verify those beneficial owners. Any transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be updated in the company's register and notified to the Registrar within 10 working days of becoming aware. The Annual Return includes a re-confirmation declaration, which directors must certify as true and correct; the registered agent must retain evidence of the underlying CDD verification for the retention period.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (directors' and shareholders' meeting minutes)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory R&D Tax Incentive (15% of eligible R&D expenditure from the 2019/20 income year), transitional residents' exemption for foreign-sourced income (generally 4 years, extendable to 8 years upon approval), and the loss carry-forward provisions subject to shareholder continuity. No preferential corporate rate concession applies within New Zealand on the basis of an 'International Company' status; all resident and non-resident companies on New Zealand-source income are taxed at the flat national rate of 28% without sub-national surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 'Income Tax Return for Companies' (Inland Revenue, New Zealand); filed electronically through the myIR secure taxpayer portal, via e-filing (e-File / eFMC), or by approved Gateway services at www.ird.govt.nz.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The IR4 return is filed once per income year (standard balance date 31 March). Provisional tax for companies is payable in three instalments per income year following the corresponding GST return cycle (quarterly).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July following the end of the income year. For an approved non-standard balance date, the return is due three months after the balance date. Provisional tax instalments fall due on the 28th day of the month following the end of each GST period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name of the International Company and its IRD number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact New Zealand registered name; a non-resident IC must first obtain an IRD number using Form IR596. The registered agent's New Zealand office address must be shown as the registered office.

Use the applicable New Zealand Business Industry Code (ANZSIC) corresponding to ISIC 8299 / NAICS 541199 for statutory company secretarial and commercial registered agent services. Do not mark the entity 'dormant' if fee-generating services were provided during the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income derived from business: company secretarial fees, registered agent retainer fees, corporate administration charges, and ancillary compliance service income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC is assessable only on income sourced in New Zealand. Fees for services performed through a New Zealand registered office are New Zealand-source income and must be returned in this box. Foreign-source income is excluded only when a specific exemption (e.g., transitional residency rules) applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenditure: salaries, rent of the registered office, professional indemnity insurance, legal and accounting costs, AML/CFT compliance costs, and licences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses actually incurred in deriving the assessable income. Related-party cost allocations from an offshore group must satisfy the arm's length standard under the transfer pricing rules and be supported by an allocation methodology.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax (total income minus total deductions), or net loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a net loss arises, the loss may be carried forward to a subsequent income year subject to the shareholder continuity threshold of 49% and the loss carry-forward classification of the relevant tax-exempt regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: Box 30 adjusted by adding back non-deductible expenditure and exempt income adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, the taxable amount is the net profit attributable to New Zealand sources. Maintain a time-and-cost apportionment schedule for services supplied to offshore clients to support the source allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax: taxable income multiplied by the corporate tax rate of 28%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No sub-national or branch surcharge applies. The 28% rate applies equally to resident and non-resident companies; tax is calculated on the New Zealand-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: provisional tax paid, resident withholding tax on interest and dividends, foreign tax credits, and imputation credits attached to inbound dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies claim treaty foreign tax credits only when the relevant DTA provides an effective credit against New Zealand tax on New Zealand-source income. Attach the tax residency certificate and supporting DTA computation to the filing record.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty from Inland Revenue: NZD 250 immediately, with a further NZD 250 for every subsequent 7-day period of non-filing, capped at NZD 1,250 per return. Late payment penalties accrue at 1% of the unpaid amount on the first day after the due date, an additional 4% if still unpaid after 7 days, and an additional 1% per 30 days thereafter up to a maximum additional 8%. Use-of-money interest compounds monthly on all unpaid assessments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on gross dividends paid by the New Zealand International Company to non-resident shareholders; fully imputed dividends carry imputation credits at the 28% company rate, lowering the effective New Zealand shareholder burden to the balance of the 33% resident withholding tax (RWT) at personal level or treaty-reduced NRWT. Non-fully imputed dividends paid to residents attract RWT of 33%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction and provide it to the New Zealand payer before the dividend payment. The payer submits IRD Form IR304 (tax treaty claim) to the Inland Revenue and files the NRWT deduction. The payer must retain the TRC, the share register evidencing ownership percentage, and any imputation credit statement for the statutory 7-year record period. Reduced rates typically apply at 15%, 10%, or 5% (or 0% on certain fully imputed dividends under select DTAs) depending on treaty wording and the shareholder's ownership percentage.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on interest paid to non-residents: 15%, reducible to 10% or 5% under most DTAs; an Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may be substituted for NRWT on interest paid in respect of public-listed debentures where the lender is non-resident. Statutory NRWT on royalties: 15%, commonly reduced to 10% for industrial/patent royalties and 5% for cultural or film royalties under the relevant DTA, subject to the beneficial ownership requirement and TRC evidence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cross-border transactions with associated non-resident enterprises aggregating NZD 2,000,000 or more in an income year are the Inland Revenue's administrative threshold for maintaining contemporaneous Local File transfer pricing documentation. Master File and Country-by-Country reporting obligations apply to multinational groups with consolidated group revenue equal to or above EUR 750,000,000. Where the aggregate transaction amount exceeds NZD 5,000,000, a full OECD-aligned transfer pricing policy and economic analysis report is required.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code as in certain offshore centres; nevertheless, the Income Tax Act 2007, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s BG 1), the reconstruction provision (s GB 1), and associated-person rules (ss GC 1–GC 14) impose a substance-over-form standard. A registered-agent International Company must evidence real premises, qualified staff, board meetings, minutes, bank accounts, and accounting records in New Zealand. If the company is wholly administered offshore and the New Zealand registered office performs no substantive secretarial function, Inland Revenue may disregard the entity, reconstruct the taxable income, or treat the arrangement as a sham, exposing the offshore shareholders to New Zealand-source income assessments and NRWT.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of secretarial or registered-agency fee income from the IR4, creation of false invoices to inflate deductible expenses, destruction or concealment of books and records during an Inland Revenue audit, or knowingly claiming treaty relief without valid Tax Residency Certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under s 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994: imprisonment for a term not exceeding 5 years and a fine not exceeding NZD 50,000 per offence (for a body corporate, a fine not exceeding NZD 500,000). Civil shortfall penalty of 150% of the evaded tax, plus late payment penalties and use-of-money interest on the full reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participated in the fraudulent filing are jointly and severally liable for the company's tax shortfall under s 61 of the Tax Administration Act 1994. Directors additionally face personal criminal fines of up to NZD 50,000, travel restraint orders, freezing of personal assets, and disqualification from managing companies for up to 10 years under s 383 of the Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company as a mere invoicing or fee-stripping shell with no employees, no physical premise, no board meetings, and no independent records in New Zealand, relying entirely on the registered agent's letterbox address while management and control are exercised offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reconstruction of the taxpayer's position under s GB 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007, resulting in additional assessable income; shortfall penalty of 100% for an 'abusive tax position'; strike-off from the New Zealand Companies Register for failure to deliver annual returns; revocation of the certificate of incorporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be made personally liable for company debts where the company traded recklessly under s 135 of the Companies Act 1993; liability for PAYE, GST, and NRWT unpaid as a 'director penalty' under the Tax Administration Act 1994; in egregious substance-abuse cases, directors face prosecution for criminal tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The registered-agent company accepting funds by credit card or wire transfer without performing customer due diligence, failing to identify the 25% beneficial owners of foreign client vehicles, failing to verify source of wealth, or failing to file a suspicious transaction report with the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty proceedings in the High Court under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009: up to NZD 1,000,000 per breach for a body corporate and NZD 200,000 for an individual. Criminal liability (for wilful or reckless conduct) carries a fine of up to NZD 500,000 and imprisonment up to 12 months for a natural person; the reporting entity's registration may be suspended or revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the company's AML programme failures where they failed to exercise due diligence; personal penalties of up to NZD 200,000 per contravention may be imposed directly on directors, alongside prohibition orders banning them from acting as directors or managers of any reporting entity for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing related offshore entities at non-arm's length values for registered-agent and secretarial services, failing to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation once the NZD 2,000,000 threshold is exceeded, or attempting to shift New Zealand-source profits to a low-tax offshore beneficiary through inflated management fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner of Inland Revenue may adjust the non-arm's length consideration to an arm's length price under ss GC 6–GC 14 of the Income Tax Act 2007. Shortfall penalties apply at 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, and 100% for an abusive tax position; late payment penalties and use-of-money interest compound until satisfaction of the reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or certify tax returns adopting artificial transfer prices may be personally assessed as directors for unpaid corporate tax liabilities; where the pricing was fraudulently documented, criminal evasion charges under s 143A may be laid against the directors individually, with exposure to imprisonment of up to 5 years and personal fines.
